negative_reviews: (1★) Hema chandran: I had a disappointing experience with the management while using this gym through my Cult Pass. The gym doesn’t have a proper Cult check-in system like QR scanning or biometric verification, so they rely on members sharing an OTP over WhatsApp. The process itself was never communicated clearly. Sometimes I was told they would call me for the OTP, and whenever they asked, I always shared it. On other occasions, they expected me to message it myself without any reminder. Instead of addressing this confusion professionally, they accused me of “using the gym for free” because some of my visits hadn’t been recorded. As a paying Cult member, that accusation was both unfair and disrespectful. If the gym’s attendance process depends on manual OTP collection, the responsibility should be shared by the management to ensure it is collected consistently. Everyone can have process-related misunderstandings, but the way they are handled says a lot about a business. A simple, polite conversation would have resolved the issue. Unfortunately, the management chose an accusatory and unprofessional approach instead. I hope they improve both their check-in process and, more importantly, the way they communicate with their members. If you’re looking for a gym where members are treated with respect and concerns are handled professionally, I would recommend considering other options. I will escalate this incident to Cult, as I believe partner gyms should maintain clear processes and treat members with professionalism and respect.

negative_reviews: (1★) Jastybhanu Ramakrishna: I visited Supes Club Gym, Anna Nagar, using a day pass that cost ₹750. At this price point, I expected a premium gym experience, but I left feeling disappointed. When I entered the gym, there were only two trainers available while around 12-15 members were working out. With so many people, it was impossible for the trainers to provide proper attention to everyone. As a first-time visitor, I expected at least a basic introduction or demo on the equipment, but no such support was provided. The gym also felt quite congested, with machines placed very close together and very little space to move around comfortably. Although the equipment is in good condition and the gym is reasonably clean, the overall atmosphere didn't feel premium. I've previously worked out at F45 Gym, where the equipment layout, trainer support, and overall environment felt much better. In comparison, Supes Club didn't meet my expectations. Paying ₹750 for a day pass without any trainer guidance or even a basic demo session is very disappointing. Good equipment alone isn't enough—proper trainer support is essential, especially for first-time visitors. I hope the management improves trainer availability and customer support so that the experience matches the price being charged.
